title: PowerPoint on Mac: reference SharePoint and OneDrive files when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The briefing passes: its release facts match the roadmap, and Microsoft documentation supports the file-reference behaviour, permission boundaries, and both control paths and commands. The feature-specific default, entitlement, and effect of Restricted Content Discovery on explicitly named files remain appropriately qualified as undocumented.

claims.quote: You can now reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph; summary; Scope: Content
claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint recognises SharePoint and OneDrive files mentioned by file or document name in a prompt.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint can now recognize references to files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive when you mention them in your prompt, such as by file or document name.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot can use the referenced file as context when creating the presentation.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph
claims.claim: Implicit references to files stored in these locations were not previously supported.
claims.quote: Previously, these implicit file references were not supported for files stored in these locations.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph

claims.where: Why it matters: first paragraph
claims.claim: The user need not first locate and manually attach the file.
claims.quote: You can bring existing SharePoint and OneDrive content into your presentation workflow more naturally, without first locating the file and manually attaching it.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The feature-specific default state is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Copilot implicit file references feature default enabled administrator setting 555897. Read roadmap record and release-notes entry; checked returned app-model and control guidance. No default specific to this capability stated.

claims.where: summary; What's changing: third paragraph
claims.claim: The roadmap record and feature release note name no feature-specific admin setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint implicit file references SharePoint OneDrive document name default admin setting license Basic meter. Read roadmap record and full feature entry in release-notes; neither names an admin setting.

claims.where: Why it matters: second paragraph
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor the feature release note specifies required administrator action.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint implicit file reference default state administrator action fetch component source write background. Read roadmap record and release-notes feature entry: it gives user Try this steps and specifies no required administrator action.

claims.where: Why it matters: second paragraph
claims.claim: The release notes describe gradual rollout to a subset of tenant users before expansion across the organisation.
claims.quote: Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot presents only data the individual can access using the underlying Microsoft 365 access controls.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot presents only data that each individual can access using the same underlying controls for data access used in other Microsoft 365 services.

claims.where: Why it matters: first paragraph; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Referencing a file does not give the user a new permission to otherwise inaccessible organisational content.
claims.quote: Semantic Index honors the user identity-based access boundary so that the grounding process only accesses content that the current user is authorized to access.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits selected SharePoint sites' discovery in organisation-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery helps you limit discovery of content from specific SharePoint sites, including recently interacted files, in organization-wide search results and Microsoft Copilot responses while those reviews are taking place.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery can be applied only to SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: You can only apply this feature to SharePoint sites.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is not supported for OneDrive sites.
claims.quote: It's not supported for OneDrive sites.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes discoverability rather than existing permissions.
claims.quote: No. Restricted Content Discovery affects discoverability, not access permissions. Users who already have access to content can continue to access it.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not state whether Restricted Content Discovery stops a SharePoint file explicitly named in a PowerPoint prompt.
claims.quote: Searched: Restricted Content Discovery PowerPoint implicit file references named prompt SharePoint. Read restricted-content-discovery and release-notes; discovery scenarios and already-in-use content are distinguished, but named PowerPoint references are not classified.

claims.where: controls[0].scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery updates take time to propagate.
claims.quote: Because the setting must propagate across indexing systems, updates can take time to become fully effective.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: For a site with more than 500,000 items, a Restricted Content Discovery update could take more than a week to fully process.
claims.quote: For sites with more than 500,000 items, an update to Restricted Content Discovery could take more than a week to fully process and reflect in search and Copilot experiences.

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraph
claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
